title: Granular retry modes, resumable streaming, and schema-evolution guidance for hybrid paging SDKs
creator: Avery Chen
description: PRD and acceptance criteria for a cross-language SDK update that introduces: (1) explicit retry modes per call (fail-fast, idempotent-safe, best-effort), (2) resumable streaming primitives with opaque resume tokens, and (3) a backwards-compatible schema-evolution policy for paginated responses and stream framing. Goal: enable product teams to adopt adaptive retry policies and resumable streams without breaking existing consumers across Python/TS/Go clients.
background_and_motivation: Multiple customers reported outages and inconsistent client behavior during transient infra failures and partial stream disconnects. Current SDKs surface coarse retry behavior and an ad-hoc streaming surface that requires application-level checkpointing. Engineering has prototype kernels for resume tokens and per-call retry metadata. PM must define requirements, compatibility guarantees, and acceptance tests to coordinate SDK and server rollout with minimal customer friction.
requirements: Introduce a per-request retry_mode parameter with three values: 'fail_fast', 'idempotent', 'best_effort'. Default remains 'idempotent' for safety.

Provide a resume token mechanism for streaming responses: server emits opaque resume_token events at natural boundaries; SDKs persist and offer resume(token) API to continue from last acknowledged item.
Define paginated-list schema versioning rules: additive fields allowed, renaming fields requires an alias header, removed fields must remain in response for one release cycle with deprecation header.
Standardize idempotency token handling across languages: SDKs accept optional idempotency_key, add x-redwood-idempotency header, surface clear docs for when to use it.
Telemetry: emit retry_mode, attempts, last_error_code, resume_token_lifetime, and bytes_streamed at the SDK layer to Console for per-customer analysis.
Provide ergonomic client methods across languages: Python async iterator with .resume(token), TS AsyncIterable with resumeToken param, Go channel-based ResumeStream(ctx, token) helper.
Graceful degradation: when server indicates incompatible schema version, SDK falls back to conservative parsing, logs a 'schema-mismatch' event, and optionally throws if strict_mode=true.

Migration path: server and hosted endpoints will support both new and legacy stream framing for 2 release cycles. SDKs must be able to consume legacy framing and prefer new resume-enabled framing when present.
out_of_scope: Changing persistent storage recommendations for resume tokens across application frameworks.
End-to-end encryption schema changes for resume payloads (handled by security team separately).
Language runtimes beyond Python/TS/Go in this cycle.
scope_changes_and_clarifications: 2026-03-02: Added telemetry requirements after Console team asked for per-token visibility (original PRD lacked telemetry).
2026-03-06: Narrowed resume token semantics to 'opaque server token' rather than embedding explicit offsets to avoid coupling to internal sharding; SDKs must treat tokens as opaque strings.
2026-03-10: Clarified that default retry_mode remains 'idempotent' to avoid surprising behavior for existing customers.
api_surface_examples:
Python sync: response = client.list_items(page_size=100, retry_mode='best_effort')
Python streaming: async for evt in client.stream_items(): process(evt)
Python resume: async for evt in client.resume_stream(token=resume_token): process(evt)

TypeScript: const iter = client.streamItems({retryMode: 'idempotent'}); for await (const e of iter) { handle(e) }
Resume: await client.resumeStream({ resumeToken })
compatibility_matrix: Server v1 (legacy framing) + SDK pre-change => supported (no resume tokens).
Server v1 + SDK new => supported (SDK consumes legacy framing).
Server v2 (resume-enabled) + SDK pre-change => degrades: no resume, but stream remains readable; SDK logs 'resume-unsupported'.
Server v2 + SDK new => full feature: resume tokens, retry modes, telemetry.
acceptance_criteria: Design sign-off from SDK leads for Python/TS/Go recorded in PRD (link in artifacts).
Unit and integration tests covering resume: resume from mid-stream using server-supplied token returns subsequent items exactly once for idempotent streams in 95% of randomized runs.
Retry modes observability: Console shows retry_mode and attempt count for 1000 test calls with expected distributions; alerts when attempts exceed threshold.
Backward compatibility: Existing client callers without changes continue to receive paginated and streaming data for at least two releases with no exceptions thrown.
Performance guardrails: added protocol framing must not increase p99 latency by more than 3% in synthetic benchmark under production-like load.
SDK ergonomics: Python, TS, and Go SDKs each provide idiomatic resume APIs and documentation examples in the README.
